findings.text: Six of the seven delivered paths -- the AGENTS.md section, section_route.py, route-modules.json and the three driver edits -- lie outside the two declared write paths (the fragment HTML and the brief's figures directory). The work is exactly what the brief asks ('Write the route section in nova/equilibrium/AGENTS.md', 'Compare the section against a fresh s1 measurement ... using the landed s1 driver'), so the defect is the declaration rather than the diff; the fragment's 'Declared and shared paths' section (docs/evidence/fragments/code-reuse-and-hot-path/hot-path-written-down.html) now enumerates each path and asks the coordinator to ratify the six with crew complete --accept-path. Answer: exempted (run r-20261122T202611168380-hot-path-written-down, coordinator ratifies).

The check prints the measurement's revision (payload['revision']) but never compares it with the tree it is checking: --root only asserts the named modules exist. A code change after the measurement that makes a route start executing a module still passes differences=0 against the stale map, so the drift the s28-handoff decision exists to avoid is invisible to the check; only a fresh job.sh re-measurement detects it. I verified the condition is not live at this head -- git diff 8d8b526ae 2b363acdd over nova/ and tests/ changes only AGENTS.md (the doc itself), so the map describes the head's code -- but the check itself cannot see that fact.

Nothing invokes this check automatically: a grep over nova/, scripts/, tests/ and docs/plans finds section_route.py named only in nova/equilibrium/AGENTS.md prose and in the evidence fragment, so the documented route can drift and no test, hook or CI target fails. The repair round records this and declines automatic invocation under the locked decision hot-path-guard: document-only, so the section's 'run the check in the same commit that changes one is a convention with nothing binding it. Answer: exempted (locked decision hot-path-guard).
